A bounded cosine residual needs explicit scale calibration: for sᵢ=hᵀeᵢ+α cos(q,tᵢ), α≥0, the text branch can change a pairwise margin by at most 2α. If collaborative margins exceed this, it cannot reverse rankings. L2 normalization bounds cosine but does not match collaborative magnitudes; LayerNorm alone does not produce unit vectors. A relevant precedent is CLIP’s normalized dot product with learned positive inverse temperature exp(a), initialized at 1/0.07; its paper specifies a maximum scale of 100. These values are precedents, not calibrated SASRec defaults. [CLIP paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2103.00020)

For an additive branch, scale and temperature are redundant when both are free: α=g/τ. A reproducible proposal is to fix τ and learn a nonnegative amplitude, or learn temperature with a fixed gate. Initialize a sigmoid gate small but nonzero; a zero multiplicative gate initially blocks recommendation gradients into the text encoder, while a strongly negative sigmoid bias slows gate learning. Normalize both text-query and item-text projections. Normalizing the collaborative branch too simplifies scale comparison but changes the baseline scorer. These are engineering deductions, not an established SASRec fusion recipe.

Without pretrained embeddings, train a shared token encoder on available titles/descriptions. Proposed objective: L=CE(sampled fused logits)+λ CE(sampled text-only cosine logits/τ_aux), optionally adding item-ID/text InfoNCE. The auxiliary term supplies text gradients even when fusion is weak; specify negatives, duplicate masking, temperatures and λ. Recformer combines masked-language modeling with item contrastive learning, but uses pretrained initialization, so its results do not establish effectiveness from scratch. Select amplitude/λ using macro validation HR@10; inspect collaborative margins, residual variance and gate evolution to verify ranking influence. [Recformer](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2305.13731)
